response.text:
Evidence supports testing the objective before increasing NextItNet depth. [On the Effectiveness of Sampled Softmax (2024)](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) connects sampled-softmax optimization to ranking performance and emphasizes temperature: excessively hard negatives can dominate gradients. [Scalable Cross-Entropy (RecSys 2024)](https://dspace.mit.edu/entities/publication/5392aca9-0bae-4176-9b3a-a8165957ba26) approximates catalog-wide CE by selectively computing informative high-scoring outputs. These results motivate multi-negative candidate discrimination, but sampled CE remains a surrogate, not direct HR@10 optimization.

Sampling details matter. [Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) shows that the always-present positive requires different treatment from sampled negatives when deriving importance corrections. [Sequential negative-sampling experiments (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) find substantial dataset-dependent tradeoffs across uniform, popularity, in-batch and adaptive samplers. Neither high model scores nor missing interactions establish that an item is truly negative. [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116) addresses false negatives using a teacher, making its mechanism unsuitable for this constraint.

Practical hypothesis: retain one NextItNet per category; compare the baseline against temperature-controlled multi-negative softmax, then a uniform/semi-hard mixture mined by that same network. Exclude padding, targets and known training positives; deduplicate candidates. Warm up with uniform negatives, then introduce moderate hardness rather than always selecting maxima. These are proposed experiments, not established improvements or reliable false-negative identification. Use training histories only for filtering and sampling, preserve the pinned evaluator, and select by macro validation HR@10. No teacher, additional predictor or inference score fusion is needed.
